scene_summary: A small tiled bedroom with a bed, white shelving and cabinet, two floor lamps, an open door, and a large white structure at the right.
overall_evidence: The reconstruction recovers many recognizable objects and their broad arrangement, including the shelves and cabinet on the back wall, lamps, a central bed, and a right-side white structure. However, the view is much wider and more distant, the open door is reduced to a narrow strip, and prominent flooring, lighting, and surface details differ substantially.

main_defects.description: The reconstruction uses a substantially wider, more distant view: the whole bed and much more floor are visible, while the reference is a close, downward view with the bed cropped by the foreground and the door dominating the right center.
main_defects.evidence: The reconstructed bed occupies a relatively small, complete rectangle; the reference bed extends beyond the bottom edge. The reconstruction also exposes a dark exterior border above and to the left of the room.
main_defects.uncertainty: Some apparent scale and spacing differences may be caused by camera position and field of view rather than object dimensions.

main_defects.description: The door presents a broad angled wooden face in the reference but appears almost edge-on as a narrow light strip in the reconstruction.
main_defects.evidence: The reference shows large inset panels on the open door; the reconstruction shows only a thin pale surface beside a dark opening.
main_defects.uncertainty: The different camera position contributes to the apparent angle; the actual door rotation cannot be determined from these views alone.

main_defects.description: The reconstruction largely replaces the reference's mottled beige and dark floor areas and pale rounded rug with a uniform gray floor, and simplifies the visible wood and woven-looking surfaces.
main_defects.evidence: The reference has a visibly irregular tan floor area behind the bed and a pale curved area beside it; the reconstruction floor is mostly flat gray with only a small pale angular patch near the bed.
main_defects.uncertainty: The exact materials and boundaries of the reference floor coverings are partially occluded.

main_defects.description: The right-side structure is simplified to a large flat rectangular panel with a small projection, whereas the reference shows a large foreground panel and a more substantial raised or sloping white section behind it.
main_defects.evidence: The visible silhouette and layered white surfaces at the right differ, especially above and behind the foreground panel.
main_defects.uncertainty: The reference object is heavily cropped and its identity and hidden construction are unclear; viewpoint may account for some of the silhouette difference.

main_defects.description: The reconstruction lacks the strong warm illumination and distinct pools of light on the rear wall around the lit lamp, giving the room flatter, cooler illumination.
main_defects.evidence: The reference has bright warm patches above and below the rear shade, while the reconstruction wall is comparatively evenly gray.
main_defects.uncertainty: Exposure and rendering choices may contribute to the difference.

strengths: The back-wall open white shelving and adjacent glass-front cabinet are recognizable and in the correct broad order.
Two slender floor lamps are present near the shelving and doorway.
The bed has a white mattress and beige base, and the room retains a light tiled wall pattern and a large white structure to the right.
uncertainty: This is an initial automated visual judgment, not a human rating or validated aggregate metric. The images have markedly different viewpoints and framing; apparent object sizes, angles and separations cannot all be attributed confidently to scene geometry. Occluded and cropped regions cannot be assessed.
